The long cane sticks are cut into smaller pieces that are followed by splitting the cane to obtain thin strips. Cane can be further split, making it as thin as required.
The split cane is now bent using a blowlamp that may cause some burns on the surface; these are removed by rubbing with sandpaper.
The cane is bended in the desired shape for a furniture or article by process of heating with blow lamp.
Following this, the cane can be woven based on the design of the articles being fashioned from it.

The whole stem of cane and bamboo is cut with a hacksaw and split longitudinally into various sizes by a billhook.
The production of cane and bamboo articles involves the cutting of whole stems with a hack saw and slicing them into splits of various sizes using a bill hook or Dao.
The craftsmen cut the bamboo into sizes of desired length with the help of cutting tools called Dao. Bamboo length cut as per thickness with the help of different kinds of knives.
The ends are joined with adhesive and nail and the joints are blended with strips of pencil cane.
The items produced in cane & bamboo are cleaned with sand-paper and polished with varnish.
Cane and bamboo furniture making starts by:
Cutting the lengthy bamboo sticks into required different sizes. It is cut into different sizes as per the size of the bamboo frame.
The cane is wrapped around the bamboo frame by weaving. This process of rounding is locally called as Binayi.
The thin cane is soaked in water until it attains moisture. The bamboo is immersed in water for 2 hours to absorb the moisture.
Artisan applies pressure on the bamboo stick for initial shaping while using the burner for the purpose.
Shaping is done with the help of wooden tool called Mungri locally. Proper shaping is obtained by shaping with Mungri.
Mungri: A wooden tool used to bend and shape the bamboo.
Cane joined to the bamboo with thin small nails.
The ends of the cane are joined using small iron nails.
The other parts of furniture are joined tightly by binding using thin cane strips.
Skilled artisan creates design pattern while weaving.
The artisan creates simple motif patterns while weaving
Thus the frame of the article is made and it is polished with sand paper to obtain smooth texture.
The burnt skin layer is removed and smoothened.
Chaaku: Knife used to scrap the burned bamboo skin to make the texture smooth.
Ari - Another type of knife used to smoothen and beautify the bamboo texture.
Jamboori (Jamura: used to pull the cane)
Hammer(Hatoda: Hammer is used during furniture making to pierce the nails)
Cutter (used to cut the thin cane)
